questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of applying patches?
options: `git apply --check` tests whether a patch appears applicable without changing files. Review patch provenance and context before applying it, then inspect the resulting diff and run project checks.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: `git apply --check` tests whether a patch appears applicable without changing files. Review patch provenance and context before applying it, then inspect the resulting diff and run project checks.
questions.explanation: `git apply --check` tests whether a patch appears applicable without changing files. Review patch provenance and context before applying it, then inspect the resulting diff and run project checks.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git apply --check change.patch` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with applying patches?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
